newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIA TRANSPORT-Oil prices seen technically vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIA TRANSPORT-Oil prices seen technically vulnerable.

text.p: --------------Analysis by Daniel Fock - Dec 12---------------
*Trading within bearish wedges
*Indicators mixed
*Could test support
The NYMEX spot light crude oil price (Wednesday U.S. close US$23.38) is trading within a potentially bearish ascending wedge.
On a break of US$23.30 traders will sell in the short term looking for much lower levels.
Short term technicals are bearish.
They are unlikely to become oversold until the index reaches US$23.00. There is some support at US$23.15/23.00.
If there is a bounce, crude is unlikely to go higher than US$25.00.
In both the short and longer terms, crude is trading within an ascending wedge.
These are potentially bearish patterns, if prices do not trade into the apex.
These are about three quarters formed and hence traders are likely to view this with trepidation.
On a break of US$23.15, the short term pattern targets US$16.98, and on a break of US$22.60, the larger longer term wedge signals US$15.86.
Medium term technicals are mixed.
The moving averages are on balance bullish, with the leading indicators suggesting some consolidation or a movement lower. In the medium term US$23.00 is a critical level.
On a break of this, traders will be looking for crude to test the top of the consolidation zone bounded by US$16.65 to US$20.85.
Longer term technicals are still showing crude in its very established bull phase since the low of US$14.49 in Feburary 1994.
However, there are signs that this bull market may be slowing.
The ROC has turned lower, the RSI is trading down, and the lower Bollinger Band has dropped dramatically over the last few months.

These technicals coupled with the ascending wedges, and the possibility of some correction of the shorter bull run, will add scepticism to the bulls. Fibonacci retracement of the 1996 bull run are US$22.62, US$21.61 and US$20.60.
Crude has failed to exceed its October high of US$25.90, and made double top resistance at US$25.70.

The two bearish ascending wedges, the short term bearish technicals and the slowing momentum in the medium and longer term suggest that crude will have some downward selling pressure in both the short and longer terms.
Traders will be cautious with the run up to Christmas, and will be holding close protective stops. Expect further selling if crude trades lower than US$23.15.
(Daniel Fock is a member of the Australian Technical Analysts Association. Views are his own, not those of Reuters.)
